title: King Oliver buys him a clarinet and he returns to it
summary: With Oliver he played tenor and soprano beside clarinetists Albert Nicholas and Darnell Howard; when they left for China Oliver bought him a new Conn clarinet and he took up clarinet again for good.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Then when you joined King Oliver --
And a friend of mine, Albert Nicholas, played clarinet. And when I joined Oliver, Albert Nicholas and Darnell Howard -- there was two clarinet players and --

-- they were in the group, so I -- and at the time they had music, if they had a little chorus, like for three clarinets, I'd play the soprano instead of the clarinet -- the part. So that's the way it went on. Then the guy wanted me to go to China.
What guy was that that wanted you to go?

A fellow from Chicago. He was taking the group to China. And I didn't want to go and I said, "No, I didn't want to go." So Albert Nicholas and Darnell went. said, "I'll go, I'll play tenor." So that left King Oliver with a lot of clarinet players, you know. So he came over to me one night, he said, "Didn't you use to play clarinet?" I said,

"Yeah, that's what I first learned." He said, "Why don't you play it?" I said, "Because I'm terrible." So he said, "If I buy you one, would you try to play it?" I said, "Sure. What have I got to lose?"

So he went downtown and bought one for me. And it was an old Conn clarinet, brand new, though. I took the thing home and (unintelligible) I started fooling around with it and I discovered that I could play more than I ever could on the clarinet. And I began to fool around with it and I began to like it again. And I woodshed -- you know, practicing -- we call it woodshedding, and I found out that it was coming around real good.

So he said, "You see, you little fool. You can play good. Why didn't you do that a long time ago?" I said, "Oh, I didn't like it like that. I didn't think I could do this kind of thing." So finally I started playing the clarinet and I put down the soprano altogether. The next thing you know I didn't want to play the tenor anymore. And so I kept on with the clarinet, and when I left Oliver and I came to New York -- and so I went to -- First I left Oliver and I went to Milwaukee with Charlie Elgar. He was from Chicago. He had a good band, too.
